name: Example: Expanding a Binomial
problem: Find the first $3$ terms in ascending powers of $a$ of the binomial expansion of $(1+3a)^5.$
worked_solution:
The first $3$ terms of the binomial expansion for ${(1 + x)^n}$ are given by

$$
{(1 + x)^n} = 1 + nx + \frac{{n(n - 1)}}{{2!}}{x^2}  +  \cdots .
$$

By substituting $x=3a$ and $n=5$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+3a)}^{5} & =1+5(3a)+\frac{5(5-1)}{2!}{(3a)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+5(3a)+\frac{5(4)}{2}(9{a}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =1+15a+90{a}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
